blockers.directSdk: Official direct Client/StdioClientTransport owns one private spawned child. It supplies no separate actor attachment; two new direct transports are not the same browser. Reuse the vendor daemon own single Client/Stdio instead for the candidate below.
blockers.scopedNativeDaemon: Source-supported candidate: hold the installed daemon/daemon.js native executable directly under the existing lifecycle owner, with fresh scoped CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_SESSION_ID and exact pinned native args. Two actual separate actor contexts invoke native exported sendCommand against that scope; sendCommand checks daemon running and does not auto-start/reconnect. Caller correlation and original actor tool returns establish who operated; no cryptographic or native LLM-identity attestation requirement is added. This internal native interface is not a documented public stability promise; Root must accept its pinned use and source/offline contract before BUILD. Runtime proof remains future, not a reason alone to label unsupported.

proposedOwnedNativeInvocation.scopeDerivation: Native utils getRuntimeHome(sessionId): Windows os.tmpdir()/chrome-devtools-mcp-<scope>; daemon.pid therein. Native getSocketPath(sessionId): Windows named pipe \\.\pipe/chrome-devtools-mcp-<scope>-<os.userInfo().username>/server.sock via native path.join. Let native utils derive paths; never call this a native returned browser session. Exclusive fresh scope/root claim and collision refusal before launch; no personal/default scope.
proposedOwnedNativeInvocation.callSurface: Each actual separate actor invokes installed exported async sendCommand(command, sessionId, timeout) from daemon/client.js through its own original native Node tool invocation. One-shot native invocation wrapper may import the pinned export and serialize its original returned envelope only; it may not implement sockets/MCP/CDP, dispatch other actors, impersonate actor IDs, or launch/retry a daemon. Exact wrapper path fixed by future source WO.
sameContextSequence: Separate future technical native-interface effect admission precedes launch or status/browser calls; no live authority exists now. Original owner exclusively claims UUID scope, holds native foreground daemon handle and records argv/env/source/version bindings.
Initial native status awaits setup and agrees with original daemon PID/startDate/version1.9.0/args/socket BEFORE any actor browser call.

Actual actor A invokes native list_pages; capture lazy-launch MCP/Chrome process/profile identity before dependent parsing; A creates/controls/captures target through native invoke_tool and actual returned page ID.

Actual distinct actor B independently invokes native list_pages and same-target observation through its own original native tool/process return; Root manually reconciles actor correlation, native page/process facts and original capture. This is provisional capability evidence only, never complete R139 G0 acceptance.

A invokes close_page for exact target; B independently invokes final native list_pages, recording target absence and baseline. Both one-shot caller handles must have their original terminal outcomes recorded, not just daemon responses.

Owner confirms same original identity before native sendCommand stop; waits original daemon handle and records original wait/exit and known daemon/MCP/Chrome absence or UNKNOWN. Only after all mandatory terminal/custody/cleanup evidence may a reviewer accept this complete native-interface capability slice.

No product operation follows under this design: held-context continuation through original R139 G0/product admission/G1/G2/E06 close/terminal remains NOT_DESIGNED. A completed native capability lifecycle closes its browser; a later product run needs separate authority and does not inherit this context or reset old campaign clocks.
failureInvariants: Native browser.ensureBrowserLaunched physically launches a new Chrome after loss; index reconstructs context. Pre/post samples, an error or reconnect notice can detect only after relaunch/action. They cannot enforce zero physical replacement or prevent an action in that race. HARD PRODUCT RELEASE HOLD until source-backed enforcement preserves the locked no-replacement requirement or an explicit Owner acceptance change is granted. No guard-as-proof.

Only native sendCommand export may be called by separate actors: no CLI start/startDaemon/ensure/version-repair/stopDaemon helper, custom browser wire or broker. Native internal Client/Stdio is daemon implementation, not caller permission.

Fresh nonempty UUID namespace is exclusively claimed; collision STOP, never adopt/delete. Minimal identical env for owner and callers omits XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/XDG_ROOT and ambient session/config/provider overrides, with consistent owned TEMP/TMP.

Initial native status awaits started and binds PID/startDate/version/args/socket to original held foreground process BEFORE browser calls. Native session scope and caller labels are correlation, not native browser/LLM attestation.
Native sendCommand internal liveness checks are counted separately from explicit bounded CIM observations and status/stop controls. Missing/unbounded counter HOLDs, uncertain call consumes its class.
On identity loss, no tool/status/stop is sent to a possibly foreign replacement. Only exact retained original handle/object cleanup is allowed; otherwise UNKNOWN/no automatic restart.
Stop acknowledgement, removed PID file, close return or exit0 alone never establish cleanup. Original owner wait/exit plus known daemon/MCP-child/Chrome chronology/absence are required or UNKNOWN.
